_comment: Capital allocation, as its own object.
WHY NOT A FIELD ON THE PROJECT. It was one: `public_funding` on each row of
projects.json. That shape can only say what one project received, and the facts do not
arrange themselves that way — one Innovation Fund call finances several projects at
once, an IPCEI decision covers a consortium, and a state aid approval is a decision
about a country before it is a decision about a plant. A field on the recipient cannot
say any of that without repeating itself once per recipient, and repeated facts drift.
So funding is a node with edges out of it:
finances   -> project:      the money arrives here
supports   -> technology:   what it is being spent on
under      -> <file>:<id>   the legal basis, as a register measure
in         -> country:      where it lands
The project keeps a rollup, and the rollup is DERIVED — computed from these rows
wherever it is shown, never stored on the project. A stored total is a second copy of
a number, and a second copy is a number that will eventually disagree with the first.
STATUS IS NOT AMOUNT. `announced`, `approved`, `signed`, `disbursed` and `withdrawn`
are five different facts about the same euro figure, and a page that showed only the
figure would let a press release read as money in the ground. Everything here is
`approved`: a grant award or a government financing decision, stated by a party to it,
with no signature or disbursement reported in the document read.
`amount` names a parameter id rather than restating a number, so an amount cannot exist
here without the sentence it was read from existing in parameters.json. Where the
source states a programme but no figure, `amount` is null and `amount_note` says so —
an undisclosed amount and a zero are different states and this file distinguishes them.
`programme` is the measure id where the register carries the legal basis, and a named
string where it does not. Norway's Longship is the live case: it is a national decision
outside the register's perimeter, so it names itself and points at no measure.
WHAT THIS MODEL HOLDS, AND WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT. Ruled 5 September 2026, after
the Innovation Fund retro-check turned two findings up that the file could not place.
IN: capital committed to BUILDING AN ADMITTED WORKS — a grant, a state aid approval, an
IPCEI decision or project finance whose recipient is a project on this platform and whose
purpose is the plant that project is. That is what the sector pages’ committed figure
means, and it is why the figure can be read as money going into the ground.
OUT: research and pilot funding. A framework-programme grant to a consortium testing a
process, or to a demonstration unit built to learn from rather than to produce, is money
spent on FINDING OUT rather than on building capacity, and the two do not add up. Summing
them would inflate every sector total by an amount that varies with how research-heavy
the industry is, which is the one thing a comparison between sectors must not do.
THE TWO FINDINGS THAT FORCED THE RULING, recorded here rather than landed as rows:
3D at Dunkirk holds about EUR 14.8 million of Horizon 2020 money for the DMX capture
pilot, and voestalpine’s H2Future at Linz about EUR 12 million for the electrolyser
demonstration. Both are real, both are traceable, and both are excluded by the boundary
above rather than by an oversight. Neither project loses its funding: 3D and H2Future are
pilots on this platform and their research money is a fact about them, which is why the
ROADMAP carries an entry for a research-funding layer that could hold it separately
instead of quietly inside a figure about building.
WHERE THE LINE IS HARD. A demonstration unit at commercial scale that also produces is a
judgement call, and the judgement is made on what the money was FOR as the awarding
document states it, not on the unit’s size. Where the document will not say, the row
does not land and the reason is written down.

funding.amount_note: NO AMOUNT IS RECORDED BECAUSE NO SOURCE READ HERE STATES ONE. The Commission's decision gives €2.9 billion across twelve Member States and 42 participants and says the split per participant follows in the non-confidential decision; Brandenburg's releases state no figure; Tesla's 10-K states none. The €1.14 billion in circulation is trade and wire press and is not admitted. It would not enter a total in any case — this row is withdrawn and therefore FUNDING_EXCLUDED.

sources.title: State aid: Commission approves €2.9 billion public support by twelve Member States for a second pan-European research and innovation project along the entire battery value chain
sources.note: THE APPROVAL INSTRUMENT, and it does not name Tesla. The release approves the second battery IPCEI, 'European Battery Innovation', notified by twelve Member States, and gives Germany's case number as SA.55831. Its text names no participant company — the 42 direct participants are listed in a graphic the page serves as an image — and it states no capacity in GWh for any site. What ties this decision to Grünheide is the Brandenburg release of the same day and Tesla's own 10-K, both below. The page itself renders by script and returns no text to a declared reader; the content here was read from the presscorner API's own JSON for this reference.

sources.title: Tesla, Inc., Annual Report on Form 10-K for 2020
sources.note: THE COMPANY TYING ITSELF TO THE DECISION, under the heading 'Gigafactory Berlin – Pending Grant': 'We have applied for a grant with the German government to improve the design, chemistry, manufacturing technology and recycling of lithium-ion battery cells for Gigafactory Berlin. The grant was approved by the European Commission in January 2021 and its implementation will be subject to a grant agreement with the German government.' The filing states no GWh for the cell plant. Tesla's FY2021 10-K carries no such heading at all — the disclosure is simply gone, which is an absence and is not recorded here as a statement.

sources.title: Tesla withdraws application for subsidies for battery plant in Germany
sources.note: THE WITHDRAWAL, AND IT IS PRESS — said so rather than dressed as an official record. It reports the federal economy ministry confirming that Tesla informed it and the Brandenburg economics ministry that it was withdrawing the IPCEI application. NEITHER MINISTRY PUBLISHED IT and Tesla did not: bmwk.de and the Brandenburg ministry's own press archives carry no release on the withdrawal, brandenburg.de's Tesla FAQ answers 403 to a declared reader, and Tesla's own FY2021 filing drops the disclosure without a sentence. See the row note.

funding.note:
APPROVED IN JANUARY 2021 AND WITHDRAWN IN NOVEMBER 2021, recorded as one row at its final status because a funding row carries one status and no history. The date is the withdrawal; the approval is dated on its own two sources above.

WITHDRAWN IS FUNDING_EXCLUDED, so this money is named and enters no total. That is the point of recording it: without the row, a reader has no way to know that Germany's largest single battery aid offer was made and refused, and with it as `approved` the register would assert live public money that does not exist.

THE WITHDRAWAL RESTS ON PRESS, WHICH IS WEAKER THAN THIS ROW'S APPROVAL and weaker than the standard asked for. Searched on 7 September 2026: no BMWK or Brandenburg ministry release on the withdrawal could be found on their own domains; Tesla published nothing and its FY2021 10-K merely stops mentioning the grant; brandenburg.de's Tesla FAQ, which reporting says addresses it, answers 403 to a declared reader. What is on file is Reuters, carried by CNBC, reporting the federal ministry's own confirmation. The status moves on it because leaving the row `approved` would be the larger error, and the tier is written here rather than hidden. It is queued for a manual retrieval of the ministry FAQ.
